body: This aligns with my understanding of how vscode and other editors do it. Left/Right just cancel the selection in that direction and by token cancels in that direction then takes the step.
why the change for the Extreme case here?
is there a reason why you didn't bake the selection printing logic into Printer? it seems generically useful

I had presumed there's a performance improvement by exiting the direction of the extreme movement rather than from the selection focus. I mostly thought about it for extreme up/down. Looks like this diverges from vs code in the multiline case for home/end. This intuitively makes more sense to me but I can move the extreme case to be with the goal one. @disconcision do you have any intuition for how it should work?
Mostly a skill issue and not wanting to figure out how the buffers work in selection.
Would you calculate it the way I am and then add selection_point to Zipper like caret_point? Mostly I'm afraid of making something wrong in the actual code vs the tests.

Just tested with prosemirror/vscode/some online text inputs. Home/End, Extreme(Left | Right), seem to always break on the caret focus direction. It doesn't make a ton of intuitive sense to me but I can change it to that.

Interestingly move left/right by token seems to just directionally cancel on prosemirror and textinput boxes, but it does move in vs code. I'm planning to stay compliant with vs code.

I spent about an hour trying to get this to work by rewriting the printer to operate over the zipper structure with the caret/selection handled throughout. It seems possible but requires a bunch of rewriting. I couldn't figure out the right way to do the selection anchor in terms of Measured so if I do this in the Printer it would just be doing this string offset trick in the of_zipper function. Not sure that's worth it.

i know i said to do it the way youre doing, which is still fine by me, it but to do it via measured, i think you just do: take the first and last pieces in the selection and look up their first/last in the measurements. use the focus to decide which is the caret. use this logic only when the selection is non-empty, still caret_point otherwise
@disconcision I think I did it but would like your review on https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/pull/1781/commits/e50db3b88b39746bdaa0614f5441e62ef27af4c8
